Purphoros, God of the Forge{3}{R} Legendary Enchantment Creature — GodEvery creature that enters deals damage to each opponent, and you make Goblin tokens two and three at a time.$31.48

Deck rarity — by stage

Base61%Fairly familiar
Tuned76%Uncommon

Modeled odds a given opponent has NOT met this commander and that stage of the build. The input is Purphoros, God of the Forge's live EDHREC play rank — 680 of about 30,000 tracked cards — read on the same log familiarity curve the rest of this catalog uses, 10.51·ln(rank) − 7.1, which puts Base at 61%. Each rung above it is raised by how far that rung has moved off the recognizable list: (100 − previous) × changed/(changed + 16), with 10 cards changed at Tuned and 9 at Maxed.

Where the hundred comes from

Singles, not a box data/master-v2.json Owned and on order $7.55 of it already here $135.22 total

Base is that hundred with the Tuned pass undone, one displaced card restored per upgrade; Maxed is it with this deck's own Bracket-3 list applied. Every rung is exactly a hundred cards and no rung repeats a nonbasic.

Why this commander

Seventeen cards make creature tokens and 20 of the 29 creature cards are Goblins. Purphoros, God of the Forge deals 2 damage to each opponent every time another creature you control enters, and Impact Tremors and Witty Roastmaster each add another point. Hordeling Outburst by itself is 6 damage to every opponent with Purphoros out, and 12 with all three of those on the table.

How it wins

Usually without attacking. Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Hordeling Outburst and Goblin Rally are 11 tokens between them, which is 22 damage to each opponent with Purphoros on the battlefield. When you do attack, Goblin Chieftain, Rundvelt Hordemaster and Goblin Trashmaster each give other Goblins +1/+1, and Shared Animosity makes an attacking swarm enormous.

Key cards

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Purphoros, God of the Forge{3}{R}Legendary Enchantment Creature — God2 damage to each opponent per creature entering, and indestructible, so removal almost never touches it.$31.48
Impact Tremors{1}{R}EnchantmentA second copy of the Purphoros trigger for two mana, and opponents rarely spend removal on it.$2.10
Krenko, Mob Boss{2}{R}{R}Legendary Creature — Goblin WarriorDoubles your Goblin count every time he taps, which is 2 damage per token with Purphoros out.$3.22
Siege-Gang Commander{3}{R}{R}Creature — GoblinThree tokens on entry and a repeatable sacrifice outlet that throws 2 damage at any target.$0.27
Goblin Bombardment{1}{R}EnchantmentFree repeatable sacrifice outlet - it converts a board that is about to be wiped into damage.$2.85
Shared Animosity{2}{R}EnchantmentEvery attacking Goblin gets +1/+0 for each other attacking Goblin, which is how the swarm actually kills.$4.47
Goblin Ringleader{3}{R}Creature — GoblinDigs four cards deep and puts every Goblin it finds in your hand, with haste attached.$0.99
Hordeling Outburst{1}{R}{R}SorceryThree bodies for three mana, the cleanest single Purphoros trigger in the deck.$0.45

How it plays, turn by turn

Turns 1-3. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet or Mind Stone, then a one-drop: Skirk Prospector, Fanatical Firebrand or Foundry Street Denizen. Impact Tremors on two is worth playing before any token spell, and Quest for the Goblin Lord starts counting.

Turns 4-6. Purphoros on four, then start dumping tokens - Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Hordeling Outburst, Beetleback Chief, Goblin Rally. Goblin Matron tutors the Goblin you need and Goblin Ringleader refills your hand with up to four more.

Turns 7+. Krenko, Mob Boss doubles the board every time he taps, Siege-Gang Commander turns spare Goblins into 2-damage shots, and Goblin Bombardment or Barrage of Expendables converts the entire board into direct damage at instant speed.

Mulligan. Keep three or four lands with a one- or two-mana play; a hand with Impact Tremors or a mana rock plus two token spells is a fine keep on three lands.

Score is the engine's 0–100 composite, not a win percentage. ± is the standard error across the six seeds; two rungs differ meaningfully only when the gap is larger than twice the combined figure.   • Flavor: twenty of the twenty-nine creatures are Goblins and a god that punishes the table for every one of them arriving. There is no gap at all between the theme and the plan.
  • Longevity: the lowest of the six. Thirty-seven lands, thirty-four of them Mountains, against an average mana value of 2.8, and only two true draw spells behind it.
  • Friendly: Purphoros hits every opponent for two every time a creature enters, and there is no way to point it at one player.

The six engine dots are read straight off the Tuned rung's measurement: average mana value for Rate, cards still stranded in hand at turn 8 for Card Adv., the average turn a won game ended for Clock, the share of turns 3–7 with an answer in hand for Interaction, mana screw plus flood for Resilience, and how often the commander actually landed for Assembly. The playstyle dots are a judgement, and the three lines above say which facts each one is standing on.

What to watch for

  • Blasphemous Act deals 13 damage to every creature, including all of your Goblins. Purphoros survives it, but only cast it when you are behind on board.
  • Interaction is thin: four removal spells (Abrade, Combustion Technique, Chaos Warp, Purphoros's Intervention) plus Vandalblast for artifacts, and nothing that answers an opposing enchantment.
  • 37 lands with 34 Mountains against an average mana value of 2.8 means you will flood. Only Big Score and Light Up the Stage are true draw spells; the rest is looting with Faithless Looting, Cathartic Reunion, Bag of Holding and Gristle Glutton.
  • Purphoros is only a creature while your devotion to red is five or more, so do not plan on him blocking or attacking - he is a damage engine, not a body.

The nine Bracket-3 swaps turn it into a one-turn kill deck: Jeska's Will and Underworld Breach let you replay Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command and Empty the Warrens in a single turn, while Muxus, Goblin Grandee, Goblin Recruiter and Goblin Piledriver stack the board and the attack.

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Core2.67Bracket 3

Upper Bracket 2 · 0 of 3 Game Changers used

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modeled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
The Maxed rung — 3 color-legal Game Changers, about $154
Game Changer$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Smothering Tithe$62Takes the ramp slot held by Bitterthorn, Nissa's Animus. Whenever an opponent draws a card, that player may pay {2}.
Rhystic Study$70Takes the draw slot held by Mystic Confluence. Whenever an opponent casts a spell, you may draw a card unless that player pays {1}.
Thassa's Oracle$22Takes the finisher slot held by Geist of Saint Traft. When this creature enters, look at the top X cards of your library, where X is your devotion to blue.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are not a shortlist — they are the cards the Maxed hundred runs. Each was tried in several slots in the list it would join, kept only where the deck did not measurably get worse over 3,000 simulated games, and confirmed afterwards on a seed the selection never saw. Prices are Scryfall market values.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Swap Agent of Treachery for Angel of Serenity if you want to keep the table friendly — you lose almost nothing.
Claude’s 5th Place

Fifth, though the single point of failure now wears boots: Swiftfoot Boots gives Brago hexproof and lets him swing the turn he lands. The structural knock survives the patch — everything still routes through one creature connecting in combat every turn, and the tax-and-flicker pattern plays more controlling than your profile enjoys.

Modeled odds a given opponent has NOT met this commander and that stage of the build. The input is Chulane, Teller of Tales's live EDHREC play rank — 2,589 of about 30,000 tracked cards — read on the same log familiarity curve the rest of this catalog uses, 10.51·ln(rank) − 7.1, which puts Base at 75%. Each rung above it is raised by how far that rung has moved off the recognizable list: (100 − previous) × changed/(changed + 16), with 0 cards changed at Tuned and 5 at Maxed.

Where the hundred comes from

Singles, not a box data/master-v2.json Owned and on order $25.11 of it already here $88.87 total

Base is that hundred with the Tuned pass undone, one displaced card restored per upgrade; Maxed is it with this deck's own Bracket-3 list applied. Every rung is exactly a hundred cards and no rung repeats a nonbasic.

Why this commander

Fifty of the 100 cards are creatures and 29 of them do something the moment they enter. Chulane, Teller of Tales turns every creature cast into a card plus a free land from your hand, so a curve of cheap bodies snowballs. Eight blink effects - Ephemerate, Momentary Blink, Siren's Ruse, Charming Prince, Mistmeadow Witch, Soulherder, Roon of the Hidden Realm and The Eternal Wanderer - re-run the best of those enter triggers over and over.

How it wins

No single card in this deck ends a game. You out-card the table and then attack wide; Arcades, the Strategist is the closest thing to a finisher, letting the eight defenders swing for their toughness while drawing you a card each time one enters.

Key cards

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Chulane, Teller of Tales{2}{G}{W}{U}Legendary Creature — Human DruidA card and a land drop off every creature spell, plus a repeatable bounce to reuse enter triggers.$6.15
Soulherder{1}{W}{U}Creature — SpiritA free blink at every end step and it grows a +1/+1 counter each time.$1.93
Roon of the Hidden Realm{2}{G}{W}{U}Legendary Creature — Rhino SoldierA second repeatable blink that works on your turn or an opponent's.$0.31
Mulldrifter{4}{U}Creature — ElementalTwo cards on entry, cheap to evoke early, and the best target for every blink effect.$0.32
Peregrine Drake{4}{U}Creature — DrakeUntaps five lands when it enters, so a blink effect on it is close to free mana.$0.27
Arcades, the Strategist{1}{G}{W}{U}Legendary Creature — Elder DragonTurns the eight defenders into attackers that hit for toughness and draws a card whenever one enters.$4.35
Ephemerate{W}InstantOne mana, rebounds for a second free blink next turn, and protects a creature from removal.$5.20

How it plays, turn by turn

Turns 1-3. Fix and ramp: Coiling Oracle, Sylvan Ranger, Farhaven Elf, Satyr Wayfinder, Farseek or Cultivate. Overgrown Battlement on two and Axebane Guardian on three tap for a pile of mana and make the five-drop happen a turn early.

Turns 4-6. Cast Chulane, Teller of Tales with a land still in hand. From there chain creature spells - Cloudblazer, Mulldrifter, Reflector Mage, Deputy of Detention, Knight of Autumn - taking a card and a land off each. Soulherder on three starts blinking the best one every end step.

Turns 7+. Loop Roon of the Hidden Realm or Soulherder on Cloudblazer, Angel of Indemnity or Peregrine Drake, use Chulane's {3}, tap ability to bounce and recast your own creature for another card, and swing once you are far enough ahead. Ancient Greenwarden doubles land triggers and lets you replay lands from the graveyard.

Mulligan. Keep three or four lands with at least two colors plus a two- or three-mana ramp creature; two lands is keepable only if one of them fixes and you also have Farseek, Cultivate or Sylvan Ranger.

  • Build-up: fifty creatures, twenty-nine of them with an enter trigger, and a commander that turns every one of those casts into a card and a land.
  • Convergence: low on purpose. Nothing here combines into a kill; the deck wins by being ahead on cards for long enough that attacking is safe.
  • Friendly: the removal is Reflector Mage and Aetherize — it bounces rather than destroys, so the table keeps its permanents.

The six engine dots are read straight off the Tuned rung's measurement: average mana value for Rate, cards still stranded in hand at turn 8 for Card Adv., the average turn a won game ended for Clock, the share of turns 3–7 with an answer in hand for Interaction, mana screw plus flood for Resilience, and how often the commander actually landed for Assembly. The playstyle dots are a judgement, and the three lines above say which facts each one is standing on.

What to watch for

  • Thirty lands is the lowest count of the six decks, and Chulane's land drop only works if a land is in your hand - you can have him online and still get only half of him.
  • The mana is thin for a three-color five-drop commander: 13 white, 11 green and 10 blue land sources before the three fetch lands.
  • Removal is soft. Reflector Mage and Aetherize only bounce; outside Cast Out, Deputy of Detention and Song of the Dryads you cannot permanently answer a big threat.
  • Nothing here closes a game quickly. Against a pod with a fast combo deck you will lose while sitting on the best board.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

All five Bracket-3 swaps add card flow and redundancy: Rhystic Study taxes all three opponents every turn, Beast Whisperer and Guardian Project stack more draw on top of Chulane, Panharmonicon doubles every enter trigger, and Teleportation Circle gives you a free blink each end step if Roon or Soulherder gets answered.

30 lands, 50 creatures, 7 instants, 6 sorceries, 2 artifacts, 4 enchantments, 1 planeswalker. Average mana value 3.21. The roles it is built from: Ramp 13, Blink 8, Card Draw 8, Removal 6, Defender Ramp 5, Utility Creature 4, Artifact/Enchantment Removal 3, Recursion 3.

Base Variant · Deck 4
Claude’s Runner-up

First Flight — Kangee

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Kangee, Sky Warden{3}{W}{U} Legendary Creature — Bird WizardFlying, vigilance, 3/3. On attack, your attacking fliers get +2/+0; on block, your blocking fliers get +0/+2.$0.29

Deck rarity — by stage

Modeled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (5457 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognize.

Precon seed

First Flight Starter Commander 2022 OOP — hunt it ~$23 $69 total
Why this commander

One card that turns a pile of small fliers into a real clock and a real wall at the same time. Attacking fliers get +2/+0, blocking fliers get +0/+2, and vigilance means Kangee is doing both every turn cycle — for one less mana than the commander it replaces.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Wingmate Roc{2}{W}{W}Creature — BirdRaid: a second Roc on the first attack, then both gain you life on every attack after. Two fliers for Kangee to pump.$0.99
Restoration Angel{3}{W}Creature — AngelA 3/4 flash flier that blinks a friend. Kangee turns it into a 5/4 attacker or a 3/6 blocker.$0.59
Isperia, Supreme Judge{4}{W}{U}Legendary Creature — SphinxMoves to the 99. Still draws a card every time a creature attacks you — just not the card the deck waits on.$0.60
Windborn Muse{2}{W}Creature — SpiritTaxes attacks against you — a real pillowfort piece.$1.49
Favorable Winds{1}{U}EnchantmentA second Kangee that nothing kills in combat: all your fliers get +1/+1, always on.$0.48
Empyrean Eagle{1}{W}{U}Creature — Bird SpiritThe anthem on a 2/2 flying body — the cheapest speed fix this deck can buy.$0.30
Cleansing Nova{3}{W}{W}SorceryModal wipe.$0.99
Sphinx's Revelation{X}{W}{U}{U}InstantDraw X and gain X. The refuel.$1.99

How it plays

Hold up answers, deploy flyers, chip in. Excellent at not-losing and mediocre at winning.

  • Convergence: almost none — it's a pile of good answers, not a machine.
  • Fortress: decent via counterspells, but nothing protects the board once a wipe resolves.

What Keith said

I have First Flight, the base cards make for a very slow deck. Not sure if the upgrades are enough to change it, hard to say. Most people run Kangee, Sky Warden as commander instead, synergizes well and not so expensive. Isperia costs way too much mana.
Good call — taken in full
  • Kangee, Sky Warden is now the commander. Five mana instead of six, and it is an anthem the whole flying team uses: attacking fliers get +2/+0, blocking fliers get +0/+2. Vigilance means it does both in the same turn cycle.
  • Isperia moves to the 99. It is still a fine card — a six-mana draw engine you cast when you are stabilised, rather than the thing the whole deck waits on.
  • The upgrade list tilts toward bodies in the air. Wingmate Roc, Restoration Angel and Dream Trawler were already in the shopping list; they are the highlights now, because Kangee rewards a wide sky rather than a single big flier.
  • Honest trade-off: Isperia's trigger is defensive card draw, which actually suits how you like to play. Kangee is faster and cheaper but wants you attacking. Keith owns this precon and says the stock deck is too slow — that is worth weighting.
  • Two static anthems join the buy list. Kangee is a 3/3 that must attack or block to pump, so Favorable Winds ($0.48) and Empyrean Eagle ($0.30) carry the anthem work when it is answered — they fix the slowness Keith describes better than another counterspell would.
  • Net cost +$1.07. $0.29 for the Kangee single plus $0.78 of anthems: $67.87 to $68.94.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

Upgrade value~$14 ea

The two dot rows score 28 cards costing about $378 in total — roughly $14 a card, or 7.4 upgrades per $100. That total is the 8 upgrades listed above, plus about 17 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$222), plus the 3 Game Changers below (~$159). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

The next cards you would buy

  • Sephara, Sky's Blade
  • Dragonlord Ojutai
  • Geist of Saint Traft

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Bracket 2
Core2.65Bracket 3
Upgraded
Upper Bracket 2 · 0 of 3 Game Changers used

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modeled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
The Maxed rung — 3 color-legal Game Changers, about $159
Game Changer$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Force of Will$59Takes the slot held by Spectacular Tactics. You may pay 1 life and exile a blue card from your hand rather than pay this spell's mana cost.
Rhystic Study$70Takes the draw slot held by Isperia, Supreme Judge. Whenever an opponent casts a spell, you may draw a card unless that player pays {1}.
Consecrated Sphinx$30Takes the draw slot held by Danitha Capashen, Paragon. Whenever an opponent draws a card, you may draw two cards.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are not a shortlist — they are the cards the Maxed hundred runs. Each was tried in several slots in the list it would join, kept only where the deck did not measurably get worse over 3,000 simulated games, and confirmed afterwards on a seed the selection never saw. Prices are Scryfall market values.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: A control deck that cannot protect its board or rebuild will keep losing games it had already won.
Claude’s Runner-up

Keith's rebuild of the deck he actually owns, and the fixes sharpened it: Kangee at five mana, Isperia in the 99, and two static anthems promoted so a 3/3 commander is no longer the only pump effect. Second because Arcades converges harder — this remains a very good pile of answers with a flight plan, not a machine.

Commander

Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (7862 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognize.

Precon seed

Any Orzhov / Knight shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$35 $41 total
Why this commander

Makes a Knight every turn for four mana, then converts a wide Knight board into targeted removal. One card that both builds the army and answers the scariest thing on the table.

Key upgrades

How it plays

The most literal version of the Round Table idea, and the mechanic does the storytelling: Aryel taps to summon another knight to the order every turn, and once the order reaches a certain size it can strike down a threat by itself. That is the ode you described, expressed as a rule rather than as art. It is also the tightest, cheapest build here — a 26-cent commander that generates a body a turn needs almost nothing else to function.

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modeled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changer$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Smothering Tithe$62Takes the ramp slot held by Orzhov Signet. Whenever an opponent draws a card, that player may pay {2}.
Braids, Cabal Minion$1Takes the creature slot held by Protector of the Wastes. At the beginning of each player's upkeep, that player sacrifices an artifact, creature, or land of their choice.
Orcish Bowmasters$47Takes the removal slot held by Danitha Capashen, Paragon. When this creature enters and whenever an opponent draws a card except the first one they draw in each of their draw steps, this creature deals 1 damage to any target.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are not a shortlist — they are the cards the Maxed hundred runs. Each was tried in several slots in the list it would join, kept only where the deck did not measurably get worse over 3,000 simulated games, and confirmed afterwards on a seed the selection never saw. Prices are Scryfall market values.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Aryel is a Human Knight, so it trades your non-humanoid art preference for the flavour payoff — same trade as the Syr Gwyn option.
Claude’s Runner-up

The efficiency king: 73% assembly from a twenty-six cent commander, knight-by-knight accumulation, removal built into the crown. First until the Quintorius restoration; second now only because 5o carries a built-in finisher and a stronger flavour story for the same money.

Trey's Build · Deck 5
Second of five in this row

Boros Graveyard Spirits — Quintorius

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Quintorius, Loremaster{3}{R}{W} Legendary Creature — Elephant ClericFill your graveyard on purpose, then exile it back one card at a time, taking a free 3/2 Spirit each time.$0.18

Deck rarity — by stage

Base88%Rarely seen
Tuned88%Rarely seen
Max92%Almost never seen

Modeled odds a given opponent has NOT met this commander and that stage of the build. The input is Quintorius, Loremaster's live EDHREC play rank — 8,839 of about 30,000 tracked cards — read on the same log familiarity curve the rest of this catalog uses, 10.51·ln(rank) − 7.1, which puts Base at 88%. Each rung above it is raised by how far that rung has moved off the recognizable list: (100 − previous) × changed/(changed + 16), with 0 cards changed at Tuned and 8 at Maxed.

Where the hundred comes from

Singles, not a box data/master-v2.json Owned and on order $66.13 of it already here $89.02 total

Base is that hundred with the Tuned pass undone, one displaced card restored per upgrade; Maxed is it with this deck's own Bracket-3 list applied. Every rung is exactly a hundred cards and no rung repeats a nonbasic.

Why this commander

Eleven cards discard or mill on purpose (Faithless Looting, Thrill of Possibility, Thrilling Discovery, Seize the Spoils, Ragged Short Spear, Conspiracy Theorist, Millikin, Advanced Reconstruction, Quintorius, History Chaser, Glittering Massif, Night Market), so your graveyard fills fast. Quintorius, Loremaster then exiles one noncreature, nonland card from it at every end step and hands you a 3/2 Spirit; sacrificing a Spirit casts that exiled card for free. Eleven more recursion cards pull permanents back, and every card that leaves the graveyard triggers Quintorius, Field Historian, Quintorius, History Chaser, Relic Retriever and Spirit of Resilience for still more Spirits.

How it wins

Moonshaker Cavalry at eight mana gives your whole team flying and +X/+X where X is your creature count, which usually kills a player outright off a board of 3/2 Spirits. Hofri Ghostforge and Balefire Liege get there the slow way, adding trample and haste and turning each 3/2 Spirit token into a 6/5.

Key cards

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Quintorius, Loremaster{3}{R}{W}Legendary Creature — Elephant ClericThe engine: a Spirit every end step, and each Spirit converts into a free spell from exile.$0.18
Moonshaker Cavalry{5}{W}{W}{W}Creature — Spirit KnightThe only real finisher in the deck - flying and +X/+X for the team turns a wide board into lethal.$9.57
Hofri Ghostforge{3}{R}{W}Legendary Creature — Dwarf ClericSpirits get +1/+1, trample and haste, and every nontoken creature that dies comes back as a Spirit copy.$0.27
Balefire Liege{2}{R/W}{R/W}{R/W}Creature — Spirit Horror+1/+1 to your red creatures and +1/+1 to your white ones, so red-and-white Spirit tokens get both, plus 3 damage on every red spell.$0.62
Quintorius, Field Historian{3}{R}{W}Legendary Creature — Elephant ClericA second Spirit factory that fires on any card leaving the graveyard, not just at end step.$0.23
Sun Titan{4}{W}{W}Creature — GiantReturns a mana value 3 or less permanent when it enters and again on every attack.$0.34
Faithless Looting{R}SorceryOne mana to load the graveyard, and it flashes back later to do it again.$0.39

How it plays, turn by turn

Turns 1-3. Land every turn and get a rock down - Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone or Mind Stone. Then loot: Faithless Looting or Thrill of Possibility puts something worth recurring in the yard. Weathered Wayfarer and Knight of the White Orchid catch you up if a land drop is missed.

Turns 4-6. Cast Quintorius, Loremaster on five and keep Selfless Spirit or Valorous Stance up to protect him. Each end step you exile a card and get a Spirit; spend the Spirits on Sevinne's Reclamation, Cast Out, Return to Dust or whatever you binned. Staff of the Storyteller turns the token flow into cards.

Turns 7+. Get to eight mana for Moonshaker Cavalry, or land Hofri Ghostforge or Balefire Liege first so the Spirits are already oversized. Sun Titan and Karmic Guide rebuild the board after a wipe; Teshar, Ancestor's Apostle reanimates a cheap creature on every historic spell.

Mulligan. Keep three or four lands with at least one untapped red or white source, a cheap mana rock or Weathered Wayfarer, and one looting spell; a hand with no way to fill the graveyard does nothing for four turns.

Score is the engine's 0–100 composite, not a win percentage. ± is the standard error across the six seeds; two rungs differ meaningfully only when the gap is larger than twice the combined figure. Pod fun is the engine's own measure of whether the other three seats got a game.

The Pod Fun rung is the bench-only build: the optimiser was allowed to spend nothing and to search only cards already on Trey's shelf, with the win rate held under 60% as a hard constraint. It came back at 57.6%.

  • Build-up: a Spirit every end step and an exile pile that only ever grows — this is the accumulation deck of the six.
  • Flavor: four different cards named Quintorius, all of them making Spirits out of the history you bury. The mechanic is the story.
  • Fortress: the weakest axis. Thirty-five lands and thirty-three creatures, and until the Bracket-3 rung buys Farewell the list has no board wipe at all.

The six engine dots are read straight off the Tuned rung's measurement: average mana value for Rate, cards still stranded in hand at turn 8 for Card Adv., the average turn a won game ended for Clock, the share of turns 3–7 with an answer in hand for Interaction, mana screw plus flood for Resilience, and how often the commander actually landed for Assembly. The playstyle dots are a judgement, and the three lines above say which facts each one is standing on.

What to watch for

  • Seventeen of the 35 lands can come in tapped and ten of them always do, so an opening hand of three tapped lands hands the table two free turns.
  • Quintorius, Loremaster only exiles noncreature, nonland cards. A graveyard full of creatures gives him nothing, so keep instants, sorceries and artifacts flowing into it.
  • Ceaseless Conflict is the only board wipe and it costs five; it does replace your own nontoken creatures with 3/2 Spirits, but you have no cheap answer to a board that goes wide before turn five.
  • Four of the 100 cards are named Quintorius and all four make Spirit tokens. With none of them on the battlefield the recursion cards still return permanents, but the deck stops producing bodies entirely.

The eight Bracket-3 swaps mostly fix the mana and add reach: Inspiring Vantage and Sunbaked Canyon replace two of the always-tapped lands, Smothering Tithe and Fable of the Mirror-Breaker add real ramp plus repeatable looting, War Room adds draw on a land, and Farewell trades Ceaseless Conflict for an exile wipe that recursion cannot answer.

Anim Pakal, Thousandth Moon$4.21Takes the slot Relic Retriever holds. A widening Gnome army on every attack - a token stream Balefire Liege pumps, giving a second win angle beside Moonshaker Cavalry.
Boros Charm$4.76Takes the slot Spirit of Resilience holds. 'Permanents are indestructible' saves the Spirit army from everyone else's wipes; the 4-damage mode closes games. Premium B3 instant.
Inspiring Vantage$2.03Takes the slot Stone Quarry holds. Enters untapped exactly when you need early plays - a strict upgrade over the tapped Quarry.
War Room$5.57Takes the slot Study Hall holds. Repeatable card draw stapled to a land - flood insurance every solid B3 deck runs.

The shape of the hundred

35 lands, 33 creatures, 7 instants, 7 sorceries, 11 artifacts, 5 enchantments, 2 planeswalkers. Average mana value 2.98. The roles it is built from: Recursion 11, Card Draw 7, Removal 7, Value Engine 7, Ramp 6, Mana Rock 5, Token Producer 4, Card Advantage 3.

The hundred is identical in every row — only which of these cards starts in the command zone changes, and the other one plays in the ninety-nine. The field is the legends already inside this deck whose colour identity covers every card in it, not every legal commander in the colours, so this answers "is the right one already here?" and not "is there a better one anywhere?". Same engine, same table, same six seeds of 20,000 games.

Honest caveat: Seventeen of the thirty-five lands can enter tapped and ten of them always do, so an opening hand of three tapped lands hands the table two free turns. Quintorius, Loremaster only exiles noncreature, nonland cards, so a graveyard full of creatures gives him nothing.

Commander

Nethroi, Apex of Death{3}{W}{B}{G} Legendary Creature — Cat Nightmare BeastMutate. When it mutates, return creatures with total power 10 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield.$2.70

Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (5451 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognize.

Precon seed

Any Abzan shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$40 $127 total
Why this commander

Mutate returns ten power of creatures from the yard at once. Not a reanimation spell — a reanimation event, capable of ending a game from an empty board.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Wall of Blossoms{1}{G}Creature — Plant WallCheap defense that replaces itself and later becomes reanimation fuel.$0.26
Sun Titan{4}{W}{W}Creature — GiantA second, repeatable recursion engine.$0.38
Unbreakable Formation{2}{W}InstantProtects the turn you go off.$1.42
Vindicate{1}{W}{B}SorceryAnswers the one dangerous permanent, early and cleanly.$0.67
Living Death{3}{B}{B}SorceryThe other mass-return button.$4.01
Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite{5}{W}{W}Legendary Creature — Phyrexian PraetorYour team +2/+2, theirs -2/-2 — and at power 4 she comes back under Nethroi's ten-power cap.$20.14
Craterhoof Behemoth{5}{G}{G}{G}Creature — BeastThe mutate turn returns the board; Craterhoof turns the board into the win.$23.77
Archon of Cruelty{6}{B}{B}Creature — ArchonEvery arrival drains, discards and kills. The premium reanimation target.$8.08
Vigor{3}{G}{G}{G}Creature — IncarnationDamage to your creatures becomes +1/+1 counters — a fortress in card form, and it wants to be in the yard.$12.21
Animate Dead{1}{B}Enchantment — AuraTwo mana: any creature out of the yard while you wait for the mutate.$7.56
Genesis{4}{G}{G}Creature — IncarnationFrom the graveyard, three mana a turn returns a creature to hand. Recursion that never dies.$8.67
Buried Alive{2}{B}SorceryPuts exactly the right three creatures in the yard — the mutate becomes surgical.$1.50
Fauna Shaman{1}{G}Creature — Elf ShamanRepeatable: trade a spare creature for the perfect one, stocking the yard as you go.$3.89
Luminous Broodmoth{2}{W}{W}Creature — InsectYour whole board comes back with flying counters — a wipe stops being a reset.$1.61
Karmic Guide{3}{W}{W}Creature — Angel SpiritReanimates on arrival, then gets reanimated later. Chain link.$0.39
Ashen Rider{4}{W}{W}{B}{B}Creature — ArchonExiles a permanent coming AND going — clean answers stapled to a reanimation target.$0.60

How it plays

A slower, friendlier Muldrotha. You block, you trade, your graveyard fills with creatures nobody is paying attention to — and none of it looks like a threat. Then one Nethroi mutate returns ten power of bodies at once, and the board goes from empty to lethal between one turn and the next. Abzan also means you can answer the growing threat early with Vindicate rather than waiting and making it personal.

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modeled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
The Maxed rung — 3 color-legal Game Changers, about $94
Game Changer$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Crop Rotation$4Takes the ramp slot held by Sifter of Skulls. Search your library for a land card, put that card onto the battlefield, then shuffle.
Demonic Tutor$62Takes the tutor slot held by Fauna Shaman. Search your library for a card, put that card into your hand, then shuffle.
Worldly Tutor$28Takes the tutor slot held by Rune-Scarred Demon. Search your library for a creature card, reveal it, then shuffle and put the card on top.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are not a shortlist — they are the cards the Maxed hundred runs. Each was tried in several slots in the list it would join, kept only where the deck did not measurably get worse over 3,000 simulated games, and confirmed afterwards on a seed the selection never saw. Prices are Scryfall market values.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Still a graveyard deck, so it shares Muldrotha's exposure to Rest in Peace — take one of the two, not both. The Capstone budget is now fully deployed here: Elesh Norn and Craterhoof are the premium mutate payoffs, Broodmoth and Vigor make wipes a bad trade for everyone else.
Claude’s Runner-up

Second, now with the budget deployed: Elesh Norn and Craterhoof are premium mutate payoffs, Broodmoth and Vigor make every wipe a bad trade for everyone else, and Buried Alive makes the mutate surgical. Still a graveyard deck sharing the flagship's hate exposure — that is the whole gap to first.

The most chess-like deck in the matrix. Kruphix is indestructible as long as your devotion holds, so your commander survives everything, and every turn you don't spend mana you are still getting richer. You hold a huge hand behind cheap walls while three opponents fight each other, and at the moment you choose, a tripled mana pool casts four things in one turn and the game ends. Nothing you do before that turn threatens anyone.

Still first, and the budget pass armed it properly: Craterhoof doubled by Yarok is the cleanest kill in the row, Thassa blinks the best ETB every end step for free, and Zagoth Triome fixes the mana. Same box as the flagship, least graveyard-dependent, highest assembly. At $142 it finally spends like a Capstone.

Commander

Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (1097 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognize.

Precon seed

Faceless Menace Commander 2019 OOP — hunt it ~$50 $160 total
Why this commander

One permanent of every type per turn, out of your own graveyard, for free. It turns the graveyard into a second hand and makes removal aimed at you close to worthless.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Sidisi, Undead Vizier{3}{B}{B}Creature — Naga ShamanETB tutor for any card. Toolbox access.$8.13
The Scarab God{3}{U}{B}Legendary Creature — GodA second reanimation track running every end step.$5.25
Grave Titan{4}{B}{B}Creature — GiantSix power across three bodies, and it rebuilds you.$0.79
Living Death{3}{B}{B}SorceryA wipe you profit from — the convergence turn.$4.01
Kokusho, the Evening Star{4}{B}{B}Legendary Creature — Dragon SpiritRestored under the full brief: dies, drains 15 across the table — and this deck replays it.$26.21
Heroic Intervention{1}{G}InstantRestored under the full brief: hexproof and indestructible for the team — the wipe answer.$15.59

How it plays

Fill the yard on purpose, land Muldrotha, then play two or three extra cards a turn forever. The most decision-dense deck of the six.

  • Longevity: excellent.
  • Fortress: the gap — it does very little before turn five or six.

What Keith said

Seems good, playing out of graveyard will be fun.
Endorsed as-is — nothing changed
  • Nothing changed, on purpose. Keith had no criticism of this one, so inventing a swap to justify the label would be dishonest. This is the build exactly as it stood, carrying his sign-off.
  • What he is endorsing is the thing this deck does that no other deck in the lineup does: four independent recursion engines running at once, so removal aimed at you mostly does not matter.
  • One addition under the full $165 Capstone brief. Kokusho, the Evening Star ($26.21) and Heroic Intervention ($15.59) — the two cards the earlier sub-$10 pricing rule stripped out — are restored. Kokusho is a 15-life swing across the table that Muldrotha and The Scarab God can replay; Heroic Intervention is the answer to the board wipe this deck otherwise just absorbs. $118.18 to $159.98.
  • The one caution still stands. A single Rest in Peace or Leyline of the Void turns eight of these cards off. If someone at the table runs graveyard hate, this is the deck that feels it.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

Upgrade value~$17 ea

The two dot rows score 35 cards costing about $601 in total — roughly $17 a card, or 5.8 upgrades per $100. That total is the 6 upgrades listed above, plus about 26 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$450), plus the 3 Game Changers below (~$94). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Core2.77Bracket 3

On the 2/3 line · 0 of 3 Game Changers used

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modeled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
The Maxed rung — 3 color-legal Game Changers, about $94
Game Changer$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Crop Rotation$4Takes the ramp slot held by Arcane Signet. Search your library for a land card, put that card onto the battlefield, then shuffle.
Demonic Tutor$62Takes the tutor slot held by Sidisi, Undead Vizier. Search your library for a card, put that card into your hand, then shuffle.
Worldly Tutor$28Takes the tutor slot held by Corpse Connoisseur. Search your library for a creature card, reveal it, then shuffle and put the card on top.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are not a shortlist — they are the cards the Maxed hundred runs. Each was tried in several slots in the list it would join, kept only where the deck did not measurably get worse over 3,000 simulated games, and confirmed afterwards on a seed the selection never saw. Prices are Scryfall market values.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Strong as built. Its two real risks are graveyard hate and dying before turn six.
Claude’s 3rd Place

Third, upgraded: Kokusho and Heroic Intervention — the two cards the sub-$10 rule stripped — are restored under the full $165 brief, taking it to $160. Four recursion engines and 5/5 Longevity stand. It stays third because eight cards still fold to one Rest in Peace and it does little before turn five; the gap to the two above is now smaller than it was.

Trey's Build · Deck 7
Third of five in this row

Orzhov Token Drain — Shadrix

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Shadrix Silverquill{3}{W}{B} Legendary Creature — Elder DragonMake white and black tokens, sacrifice them, and drain all three opponents one point at a time.$0.34

Deck rarity — by stage

Base76%Uncommon
Tuned85%Rarely seen
Max89%Rarely seen

Modeled odds a given opponent has NOT met this commander and that stage of the build. The input is Shadrix Silverquill's live EDHREC play rank — 2,697 of about 30,000 tracked cards — read on the same log familiarity curve the rest of this catalog uses, 10.51·ln(rank) − 7.1, which puts Base at 76%. Each rung above it is raised by how far that rung has moved off the recognizable list: (100 − previous) × changed/(changed + 16), with 9 cards changed at Tuned and 6 at Maxed.

Where the hundred comes from

Singles, not a box data/master-v2.json Owned and on order $14.92 of it already here $68.47 total

Base is that hundred with the Tuned pass undone, one displaced card restored per upgrade; Maxed is it with this deck's own Bracket-3 list applied. Every rung is exactly a hundred cards and no rung repeats a nonbasic.

Why this commander

Twelve cards make creature tokens - Spectral Procession, Lingering Souls, Raise the Alarm, Clachan Festival, Ministrant of Obligation, Ophiomancer, Dreadhorde Invasion, Hidden Stockpile and more - and six drain payoffs turn those bodies into damage. Corpse Knight and Elas il-Kor, Sadistic Pilgrim drain when creatures enter; Cruel Celebrant, Zulaport Cutthroat, Nadier's Nightblade and Bastion of Remembrance drain when they die. Four sacrifice outlets (Viscera Seer, Zack Fair, Village Rites, Deadly Dispute) let you cash the board in whenever you want.

How it wins

Death triggers, not combat. With Cruel Celebrant, Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance on the table, your own Day of Judgment or Promise of Loyalty drains every opponent for the size of your board, and Teysa Karlov doubles all of those triggers.

Key cards

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Shadrix Silverquill{3}{W}{B}Legendary Creature — Elder DragonA 2/5 flier with double strike whose combat trigger hands out two of three modes each turn - one for you, one for an opponent.$0.34
Teysa Karlov{2}{W}{B}Legendary Creature — Human AdvisorDoubles every death trigger in the deck and gives your tokens vigilance and lifelink.$2.67
Bastion of Remembrance{2}{B}EnchantmentAn enchantment version of the drain payoff, so board wipes cannot remove it.$0.36
Cruel Celebrant{W}{B}Creature — VampireTwo mana, drains for every creature or planeswalker you lose, and cheap enough to recast right after a sweeper.$1.68
Skullclamp{1}Artifact — EquipmentOn a 1/1 token it kills the token and draws two, which also turns on every death trigger you control.$5.89
Spectral Procession{2/W}{2/W}{2/W}SorceryThree fliers for three white mana - the single best token spell in the list.$0.33
Viscera Seer{B}Creature — Vampire WizardThe only free, repeatable sacrifice outlet, which is what makes the drain payoffs work on demand.$0.41
Requiem Angel{5}{W}Creature — AngelEvery non-Spirit creature you lose becomes a 1/1 flying Spirit, so a wipe leaves you with a board.$0.84

How it plays, turn by turn

Turns 1-3. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Orzhov Signet or Mind Stone, then a cheap drain body on two: Corpse Knight, Cruel Celebrant, Elas il-Kor, Sadistic Pilgrim or Zulaport Cutthroat. Viscera Seer on one is the free sacrifice outlet you want down early.

Turns 4-6. Pour tokens into the payoffs. Spectral Procession costs three white mana for three fliers, Lingering Souls gives four bodies across two casts, and Raise the Alarm goes at instant speed. Teysa Karlov on four doubles every death trigger. Shadrix Silverquill on five gives you a mode every combat.

Turns 7+. Equip Skullclamp to 1/1 tokens for two cards each, then sacrifice the board with the drain payoffs out. If the board is even and you have two or more payoffs down, Day of Judgment or Promise of Loyalty is a win condition rather than a reset.

Mulligan. Keep three or four lands with both colors plus a two-mana drain creature or a cheap token maker; with 42 lands, a hand of five lands and one spell should be shipped.

The four rungs, measured

Every rung is the exact hundred this page publishes for it, played 120,000 times — six independent seeds of 20,000 games each — against the mixed pod in sim/opponents.json. Score is the engine's 0–100 composite, not a win percentage. ± is the standard error across the six seeds; two rungs differ meaningfully only when the gap is larger than twice the combined figure. Pod fun is the engine's own measure of whether the other three seats got a game.

The Pod Fun rung is the bench-only build: the optimiser was allowed to spend nothing and to search only cards already on Trey's shelf, with the win rate held under 60% as a hard constraint. It came back at 58.0%.

  • Convergence: a drain payoff, a sacrifice outlet and a board of tokens are three separate halves, and the turn all three are down your own board wipe becomes a win condition.
  • Friendly: the lowest of the six alongside Purphoros. Every point of damage this deck deals hits all three opponents at once, whoever they are.
  • Longevity: Requiem Angel turns every creature you lose into a Spirit and Bastion of Remembrance is an enchantment a sweeper cannot touch, so the deck comes back from a wipe better than most.

The six engine dots are read straight off the Tuned rung's measurement: average mana value for Rate, cards still stranded in hand at turn 8 for Card Adv., the average turn a won game ended for Clock, the share of turns 3–7 with an answer in hand for Interaction, mana screw plus flood for Resilience, and how often the commander actually landed for Assembly. The playstyle dots are a judgement, and the three lines above say which facts each one is standing on.

What to watch for

  • 42 lands against an average mana value of 2.7 is roughly seven too many. Flooding out is the most common way this deck loses.
  • Viscera Seer is the only free repeatable sacrifice outlet. Village Rites and Deadly Dispute are one-shots, Zack Fair sacrifices only itself, and Hidden Stockpile costs {1} each activation.
  • Shadrix makes you choose two modes on two different players, so an opponent gets a 2/1 flier, a card, or counters every combat. Give the draw-and-lose-1-life mode to whoever is furthest behind.
  • Only 26 of the 100 cards are creatures. If the token makers get answered, the six drain payoffs have nothing to eat.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

Headroom6 cards
Upgrade value~$17.96 ea

The Tuned swaps are already applied in this list: Skullclamp, Teysa Karlov, Requiem Angel, Day of Judgment, Ossification, Mentor of the Meek, Night's Whisper and Elspeth, Sun's Nemesis are in, and eight weaker cards including Costly Plunder, Suture Priest and Inspiring Overseer went to the bench. The seven Bracket-3 swaps add exactly what is thin: Blood Artist and Dictate of Erebos as more death payoffs, Ashnod's Altar and Pitiless Plunderer as free sacrifice outlets, Elenda, the Dusk Rose as a wipe-proof threat, and Anointed Procession to double every token you make.

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Game Changers in the Maxed hundred
  • None — this deck's own Bracket-3 list adds no Game Changer, so even its Maxed hundred stays inside Bracket 2's card pool.
The Maxed rung — 6 swaps, about $107.76
Card$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Dictate of Erebos$19.00Takes the slot Chocobo Knights holds. Flash edict engine: every token you sacrifice forces EACH opponent to sacrifice - repeatedly eats the pod's commanders and voltron threats.
Anointed Procession$59.34Takes the slot Aetheric Amplifier holds. EVERY token doubled - Shadrix makes 4 fliers a combat, Lingering Souls makes 4, Spectral Procession 6. The defining B3 token payoff.
Elenda, the Dusk Rose$5.75Takes the slot Court Street Denizen holds. Grows with every death and dies into a Vampire army - a token wincon that shrugs off board wipes.
Ashnod's Altar$16.60Takes the slot Dawn-Blessed Pennant holds. Tokens become 2 mana each - with Procession and Plunderer it empties your whole hand in one turn.
Brightclimb Pathway // Grimclimb Pathway$4.74Takes the slot Scoured Barrens holds. Untapped either side, your choice - cuts the tapped-land drag in a 2-color deck that should never stumble.
Pitiless Plunderer$4.21Takes the slot Zack Fair holds. Every dying token pays you a Treasure - sacrifice loops go mana-positive.

The shape of the hundred

42 lands, 26 creatures, 10 instants, 6 sorceries, 9 artifacts, 6 enchantments, 1 planeswalker. Average mana value 2.71. The roles it is built from: Token Producer 12, Removal 7, Drain Payoff 6, Card Draw 5, Mana Rock 5, Tuned add 4, Sacrifice Outlet 4, Board Wipe 2.

The hundred is identical in every row — only which of these cards starts in the command zone changes, and the other one plays in the ninety-nine. The field is the legends already inside this deck whose colour identity covers every card in it, not every legal commander in the colours, so this answers "is the right one already here?" and not "is there a better one anywhere?". Same engine, same table, same six seeds of 20,000 games.

Honest caveat: Forty-two lands against an average mana value of 2.7 is roughly seven too many, and flooding out is the most common way this deck loses. Viscera Seer is the only free repeatable sacrifice outlet, and only twenty-six of the hundred cards are creatures — answer the token makers and the six drain payoffs have nothing to eat.
Third of five in this row

The only one of the six whose Tuned rung actually buys something: nine cards, Skullclamp and Teysa Karlov among them, for about twenty-six dollars. That is also the largest measured step any of these decks takes for money.
